text:
maria: heads-up — seeing a large retry spike and very uneven traffic across endpoints for svc/gpu-infer in us-east around 13:02 PDT. Errors/timed out requests and lots of 502s from the app layer.
kevin: sending to #oncall? can you grab ipvs stats and svc endpoints? first guess is ipvs hash or connstick mismatch.
infra-bot: alert: svc/gpu-infer retry_rate 4.6x baseline (13:02:10 -> 13:07:00), p95 latency 640ms :rotating_light:
maria: on it, already looked at k8s endpoints — they look fine (all ready). pod CPU okay. but traffic is landing heavily on 2 pods out of 12.
samir: can you paste ipvs table from one of the node proxies? run: `ipvsadm -Ln --stats`
maria: pasted from node-1:
```
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.96.40.12:80 rr
  -> 10.10.5.11:8080               Masq    1      812      22
  -> 10.10.5.12:8080               Masq    1      28       3
  -> 10.10.5.13:8080               Masq    1      10       1
  -> 10.10.5.14:8080               Masq    1      14       0
```
maria: node-1 shows one backend with 800+ active conns, others tiny.
kevin: that smells like connection pinning: some source IPs are hashed to single endpoint. Are clients coming from a small NAT pool?
olga: we run a shared egress NAT for that VPC in us-east with 6 SNAT IPs. if some paths are asymmetric maybe the return packets take a different path and break conntrack. check kernel logs for RFC791 fragmentation/icmp frag-needed.
samir: grabbed tcpdump from node-1 (filtered):
```
13:03:05.123 IP 10.100.7.50 > 10.10.5.11: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
13:03:05.130 IP 10.10.5.11 > 10.100.7.50: Rst  ack 1
13:03:05.131 IP 10.100.7.50 > 10.10.5.12: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
```
samir: also saw `ICMP frag needed` messages on node-4 kernel: `IP: local 10.100.7.50 dest 10.10.5.11 next hop 10.200.1.1: fragmentation needed and DF set`
maria: interesting — different nodes report different MTU/fragmentation behavior. we recently added a new transit VLAN (10.200.x) to offload RDMA traffic to a dedicated fabric. might be asymmetric routes between the kube-proxy nodes and the worker subnets.
kevin: asymmetric routing + DF bit + ipvs Masq mode can cause packets to be SNATed on egress node but replies go back via another path where conntrack/affinity isn't present -> connection resets and new connections flood the one that sees SNAT.
oncall: recommended mitigation: switch Service to externalTrafficPolicy: Local? that only helps external LB case. For clusterIP we should try setting kube-proxy to `--masquerade-all`? but that's global. Alternatively, we can pin source IP by enabling `--ipvs-scheduler=sh`? not sure.
olga: kube-proxy has `--ipvs-scheduler` options but the real issue is asymmetric underlay. short term: set `net.ipv4.ip_forward=1` consistent and ensure MTU consistent on transit VLANs; increase MTU on overlay? also disable DF on the path is not an option.
samir: quick experiment: enabled `--masquerade-all` on kube-proxy on a couple nodes and restarted kube-proxy pod there; observed distribution flattening within 30s and retries dropped to baseline.
maria: logs after change show active conns across many endpoints, and retry alert resolved. can we make masquerade-all default cluster-wide?
kevin: cost: masquerade-all increases CPU on nodes (more NAT) and can affect perf for high throughput GPU infer. but if asymmetry persists we pay in retries/latency anyway. propose short-term toggle to reduce user impact and schedule network team to fix asymmetric routes and MTU. filing a ticket for infra network.
maria: created ticket NET-1129 with traceroutes, tcpdumps, ipvs dumps, and kernel logs. tagging network: @olga please coordinate.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: kube-proxy config change applied to 6 nodes (masquerade-all=true) at 13:25. rollout succeeded.
olga: network follow-up — found that new RDMA VLAN had MTU 9000 but the transit gateway to some racks was 1500, fragment needed on path for some node pairs. routed some workers via the 1500 MTU transit depending on AS path. I'm scheduling MTU normalization and a BGP policy fix to avoid asymmetric next-hops.
maria: thanks. keeping watchers — will reopen if retries climb. :thumbsup:
